Hi Elena / team —

Technical acceptance tests (proposed) — we kept them minimal and automatable so you can reproduce independent of Redwood. All pass thresholds are negotiable but proposed to reduce ambiguity at decision time.

1) Latency & Throughput- Test: 5-minute steady-state load at target QPS reflecting peak triage traffic (we suggest 50 QPS).- Pass: observed p95 <= 500 ms, p99 <= 900 ms, no request errors > 0.5%.- Owner: Soojin (SE) runs the load harness; Grace monitors.

2) Fidelity / Model Quality- Test: Run golden set (n=1,200 labeled triage utterances) through the endpoint in evaluation mode.- Pass: Macro F1 >= 0.85; hallucination incidents <= 1% (manual sample review of 200 random outputs).- Owner: Karthik supplies labeled set; Orbital assesses results with Redwood support.

3) Stability / Resource Usage- Test: 12-hour soak with mixed traffic (80% inference, 20% background batch jobs).- Pass: No OOM or node restarts; sustained < 5% error budget used; tail latency drift < 20% compared to baseline.- Owner: Soojin runs soak; Redwood infra team monitors logs.

4) Security / Observability- Test: Audit log visibility for user tokens and request traces; evidence of retention policy applied for 30 days.- Pass: Audit log entries present for all requests; access logs available to Orbital via S3 bucket link.- Owner: Grace to validate logs and share sample CSV.

5) Cutover / Fallback test (smoke)- Test: Simulate a degraded model variant fallback and confirm automatic routing occurs with < 2s switch time.- Pass: Fallback triggers and routing observed in tracing; no data loss.- Owner: Soojin + Orbital engineer (Tom).

I'll add short runbooks for each test into the shared Drive link. If you want us to lower p95 target to 350ms we can show a quantized variant but that will require a separate run and cost evaluation.
